newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet values steady to firm, paper pressured.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet values steady to firm, paper pressured.

text.p: North Sea crude remainded mixed on Wednesday with Ekofisk and Oseberg done at stronger differentials in a slow spot market while outright values and Brent CFDs looked pressured, traders said.
An Ekofisk loading June 5-7 changed hands at Dated +18 cents, a big rise from the last trade of a late-June Ekofisk rumoured done last week at a five cent discount.
An Oseberg loading July 4-6 moved at Dated +10 cents, well above the level of a Monday trade at Dated evens.
Forties was offered at Dated +30 cents and bid at +20, with little prospect of a compromise in the mid-20s, one trader said.
Two Statfjord cargoes traded on Tuesday at firmer premiums to Dated Brent. The first, due to load July 6-8 fetched Dated Brent +23 cents and the second Dated Brent +30 cents.
Some traders said other grades followed suit but others said Statfjord benefitted from its fixed freight costs as tanker rates in northwest Europe showed signs of rising.

"The market looks balanced. Sellers aren't panicking but neither are buyers," said one crude trader, adding clearer insight into North Sea market direction would come only when the prices of further Statfjord trades became known.
Nevertheless traders said that, overall, good demand for early July cargoes and thinner than expected loading programmes for the main North Sea systems bolstered spot market sentiment.
Intermonths were mixed, with July/August steady on -18/-16. August/September was down two cents at -18/-16 and September/October -14/-11 cents.
Brent CFDs showed strain for next week, talked down three cents at August Brent -35/-30. The following week was -35/-32.
The front month August contract for IPE Brent futures were under pressure, 18 cents adrift at $17.90 a tonne after a weaker New York opening.
The weakness followed American Petroleum Institute (API) reported builds in gasoline and distillate stocks last week.
Crude imports also reached record levels, the API said.
